vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: secretary-memory
Version: 1.0.0

The 'secretary-memory' skill is a complex system designed to organize and archive OpenClaw session logs into a structured directory. It includes scripts for real-time file monitoring (realtime_monitor.py), automated archiving (consolidate.py), and user preference extraction (profile_miner.py). The system performs extensive file system operations, including moving, renaming, and creating symlinks within the memory directory. Notably, realtime_monitor.py uses subprocess.run to execute system utilities like 'fuser' and 'lsof' to detect file locks, and profile_miner.py automatically extracts information such as emails and technical backgrounds from session logs. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of a 'secretary-style' memory system, the use of system-level utilities and automated PII extraction represents a high-risk surface area without clear malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill's name, description, runtime instructions and included scripts are coherent: they implement a local multi-partition memory system that reads/writes a workspace directory and provide tooling for summarization, searching, archiving, migration and preference extraction — no network or secret access is requested by the package itself.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md align with the stated purpose (multi‑partition secretary-style memory): scripts implement summarization, context loading, multi‑partition search, consolidation/archival, migration, conflict detection and profile mining. No unrelated credentials or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to run the bundled Python scripts and to configure hooks/crons that invoke them. The scripts operate against a local memory directory (default: /root/.openclaw/workspace/memory), read and write Markdown/JSON files, and accept user-specified file paths for some operations (e.g., --file arguments). This is consistent with the skill’s purpose, but the recommended hooks (daemon/crons) create persistent monitoring processes that will continuously read/write the memory area — review those if you do not want a background process touching files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only installation). Code files are included in the bundle but the skill does not download or execute remote artifacts. No external package downloads or archive extraction are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. Scripts use a single configurable workspace path (OPENCLAW_MEMORY_DIR) and otherwise operate on local filesystem content. That is proportional to a local memory management tool. Note: some scripts can read a user-provided file path (e.g., profile_miner.py --file), which is expected for their function.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). However SKILL.md recommends hooks that launch a realtime_monitor daemon and cron entries; those would give the skill persistent processes that run on schedule. Autonomous model invocation is allowed (platform default) — combine that with the daemon recommendation if you want tighter control over when the skill runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears internally consistent with its stated purpose and does not request network access or credentials. Before installing or enabling hooks, consider the following: (1) review the realtime_monitor.py, restore.py and session_summary.py scripts (they are recommended as daemons/hooks) to confirm you are comfortable with persistent background processes that will read/write the memory directory; (2) set OPENCLAW_MEMORY_DIR to a dedicated, sandboxed folder (not /root or system directories) so the skill only touches an isolated workspace; (3) backup any existing memory data before running migration/consolidation, since those scripts move files and create archives; (4) be aware the profile miner extracts PII-like data (names, emails) into local files — review retention and access policies if this matters; (5) if you want extra safety, run the scripts manually first (dry-run modes are supported) rather than enabling automatic hooks/cron entries. If you want, I can inspect the remaining bundled files in full (realtime_monitor.py, restore.py, session_summary.py) to raise any file-specific concerns — I noted portions of the package manifest were truncated in the provided content, so a quick review of those files would raise my confidence to high.
